summary: atip.codeexit.01 and .05 are under-proved. 01 (`each call that the table refuses before it starts`, brief F1: every refusal code has a real call that exits 2 with no data and leaves the work tree and .canon/ unchanged) runs two calls, BRIEF_APPROVAL_REQUIRED and TASK_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED; EVIDENCE_NOTE_INVALID, EVIDENCE_CONTRACT_CONFLICT, EVIDENCE_REPORT_CONFLICT, POLICY_APPROVAL_STALE, TASK_EVIDENCE_INVALID, STRATEGY_EVALUATION_INVALID, STRATEGY_PROMOTION_INVALID, DIVERGENCE_INVALID, CONTEXT_OBJECT_CONFLICT and DISPATCH_RUN_UNAVAILABLE have no binary-level no-data/no-write check, and a gate-wide guard that no exit-2 envelope carries `data` does not exist (print_failure_with_meta accepts data for any code). 05 is a test that searches evidence.rs for the text `judge_evidence_body(body)` before a `let` line; it does not run a batch. The behaviour is proved by unit test `evidence_add_115_*` under another name. Add a debug assertion in the failure printer that a code with exit 2 has no data, run each refusal of the table in 01, and name a land_batch test for 05 (a binary-level batch cannot make the gate refuse a body the CLI builds, so the function-level test is the right one).
